paper_id: Lin et al. - 2017 - Revisiting Reading Rate with Mobility Rate-Adaptive Reading in COTS RFID Systems
title: Revisiting Reading Rate with Mobility: Rate-Adaptive Reading in COTS RFID Systems
motivation: RFID reading rate too low when many tags present; motion tracking requires high sampling rate but COTS systems suffer from channel contention
problem_framing: Improve IRR for mobile tags by discriminating them from stationary tags; frame as rate-adaptive reading problem not anti-collision problem
key_insight: Only <20% tags are moving; stationary tags don't need high reading rate since states unchanged; cut their readings to prioritize mobile tags
method_signature: Two-phase reading: Phase I assess motion via GMM, Phase II selectively read mobile tags via Gen2 Select bitmask
evaluation_criteria: IRR gain (reading rate ratio), detection accuracy, tracking trajectory precision
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: When mobile tags exceed 20%, scheduling overhead counteracts gains; system should switch back to reading all
evidence_for_taste: only a few tags (<20%) are actually in motion
leaves very limited room to improve
current anti-collision algorithm is already a good algorithm
we are the first to accurately model the IRR
thinking_moves: 把通信问题重新frame成感知问题：非均匀分配读取资源
从真实trace数据发现只有小部分标签在移动
先建立理论下界(IRR model)，再证现有协议已near-optimal
用multipath物理模型(GMM)解决相位测量误差问题
把bitmask选择问题建模为集合覆盖问题
